video_title: THE LAST TEN - Lil Baby x Jaylen Brown

quotes.speaker: Jaylen Brown
quotes.summary_phrase: Jaylen Brown on his career transformation leaving the Boston Celtics
quotes.excerpt: I'm at a big transformation in my career, in my life. I'm about to be 30, switching teams.
quotes.quote: What does it mean to be a decade in? That's a great question because I'm at a big transformation in my career, in my life. I'm about to be 30, switching teams, leaving the Celtics. I mean, I've been there for 10 years. Now I'm going into a new city, new team, new organization, new emotions, new chapter. So it's a lot of emotion. On one end, it's sad to go, but on the other end, I'm super excited for what the possibilities are. So it's just a lot of emotion.

quotes.speaker: Lil Baby
quotes.summary_phrase: Lil Baby on the transition from being a kid to a man
quotes.excerpt: from being a kid, because I still call it a kid in your 20s, to becoming a man
quotes.quote: Just from being a kid, because I still call it a kid in your 20s, to becoming a man in your 30s, that's a mean journey within itself to me because now I got to think different. I feel like I'm living different. Watching my health, doing different things that I wasn't even thinking about in the first 10 years. Then now, it's more so like I can look at 10 years. I'm in a position now where I can look back and look over the decade. I can see some of the mistakes I made. I can see some of the right things I did, and now I can better prepare for my next 10 years.

quotes.speaker: Lil Baby
quotes.summary_phrase: Lil Baby on the importance of hard work and inspiring others
quotes.excerpt: I wanted to really make hits and really make music that inspired people and changed their lives.
quotes.quote: When I first started, I didn't want to just be a rapper and then people from Atlanta just know me as Lil Baby and stuff. So it was just cool. I wanted to really make hits and really make music that inspired people and changed their lives. So now, when I'm out places, because I build a lot of places by myself just on the regular, when people walk up to me and explain to me what a song did for them in that time in their life, and how they, how they, somebody might tell me, I listen to this song every day, it really helped me get through it. I'm most proud about that.

quotes.speaker: Jaylen Brown
quotes.summary_phrase: Jaylen Brown on the influence of Atlanta on his mindset
quotes.excerpt: Atlanta shaped my whole mentality because it's so much that has come out of Atlanta.
quotes.quote: Atlanta shaped my whole mentality because it's so much that has come out of Atlanta, culturally, civil rights, so much has come out of Atlanta. And growing up and being a part of it, I mean, I'm from the west side. I'm from the heart of Atlanta. Even though I haven't, I didn't actually, never seen a Michael Vick, I never seen a Dominique Wilkins or know them, but just to be where they was at and everybody talking about it and you're seeing, you're like your T.I.'s back then and your Young Jeezy, like you feel like you know them. You know what I'm saying? Like everything they was doing, you feel like you was a part of. Even though I didn't actually know them, but I feel like all that shaped the form who I am today.

quotes.speaker: Jaylen Brown
quotes.summary_phrase: Jaylen Brown on the importance of discipline for the next generation
quotes.excerpt: I'm going to be honest, I'm going to say discipline. There's so many things that's testing your discipline.
quotes.quote: If I'm going to be honest, I'm going to say discipline. I don't got kids, but if I were to have a son, or even a daughter too, I think that was like one of the most important things to give someone that's a young person, especially in the world that it is today, because there's so many things that's testing your discipline. There's so many distractions from the money, cars, the clothes, social media, the algorithm just put everything right in front of your face, everything that you want. You got to have a strong mind to be able to say no. You got to have a strong mind to be able to have values and respect for yourself, because this lifestyle can take you down roads you never thought you could easily that you never even thought that you could imagine as a man or woman.

quotes.speaker: Lil Baby
quotes.summary_phrase: Lil Baby on the difference between success and human change
quotes.excerpt: you don't live different. You still put on your pants the same way I do.
quotes.quote: Me personally, I care for it, you know, that's what I'm aiming for. But it's not like human changing, meaning like you don't live different. You still put on your pants the same way I do. It's like you would think like when you get the success you live a completely different life or like you you you you would think that it's supernatural almost. Like when you're successful it's like I can turn the water red or something. You know, like but it's not that. You're not a superhero. You're not a superhero. You're still a human being.

quotes.speaker: Jaylen Brown
quotes.summary_phrase: Jaylen Brown on the evolution of his definition of success
quotes.excerpt: taking care of your family, handling your responsibilities, taking care of your mom, your grandparents, that's success.
quotes.quote: As I started to grow up and realize what matters most, you know, I started to realize like taking care of your family, handling your responsibilities, taking care of your mom, your grandparents, that's success. And then you take it a step further, being able to help other people's families, other people in the community, you know what I mean, create jobs, create motivation for other people to be able to get through whatever it is that they're doing. That's success. I feel like that's the best feeling of success.

quotes.speaker: Jaylen Brown
quotes.summary_phrase: Jaylen Brown on his experience representing himself in contract negotiations
quotes.excerpt: I represented myself my first eight years in the league. I'm on the phones, I'm sending emails.
quotes.quote: Coming into the to into my 10 years, not having an agent, not having PR team, not having a marketing team, I was doing everything myself. So it was a lot of, mind you, it was a lot of work. Like I'm the one following up with emails, I'm the one and I probably missed out on some opportunities because I didn't follow up or I didn't do something, but it taught me. I learned a lot though doing it myself. I learned a whole lot.

quotes.speaker: Jaylen Brown
quotes.summary_phrase: Jaylen Brown on the importance of being in the driver's seat
quotes.excerpt: They're supposed to be helping you get to where you want to go, but you got to be
quotes.quote: They're supposed to be helping you get to where you want to go, but you got to be in the driver's seat. You can't be in the backseat in your own car. Be in the driver's seat in your car. You should be telling your team what you want from them and where you want to go.

quotes.speaker: Jaylen Brown
quotes.summary_phrase: Jaylen Brown on the value of hiring people you can learn from
quotes.excerpt: If you're hiring people, hire people that you can learn from, so at least you're getting your investment back.
quotes.quote: If you're hiring people, hire people that you can learn from, so at least you're getting your investment back. A lot of times, you know, people can do the job, you know, but nobody really want to work for real, especially in today's time, people want to do the least amount of work, get the most amount paid. And I get it. You know what I mean? It's just the world we live in. But if you're going to be hiring people and you're going to be trying to start a vision, hire people that you can learn from, so at least you're getting your investment back.

quotes.speaker: Jaylen Brown
quotes.summary_phrase: Jaylen Brown on protecting authenticity in the face of industry pressure
quotes.excerpt: How do you protect your authenticity and how do you deal with the expectations and the opinions?
quotes.quote: How do you protect your authenticity and how do you deal with the expectations and the opinions of others and maybe the industry that may be trying to push you to change or push you to do things differently? It's crazy you ask that because my next question for you is standing up for what you believe in.

quotes.speaker: Lil Baby
quotes.summary_phrase: Lil Baby on the necessity of playing the game to achieve goals
quotes.excerpt: I consider it like I'm playing a game. At times I do have to play the game.
quotes.quote: I consider it like I'm playing a game. At times I do have to play the game in a way that might not be all the way authentic to myself, but at the end of the day my self knows like what I'm trying to accomplish.

quotes.speaker: Jaylen Brown
quotes.summary_phrase: Jaylen Brown on the necessity of breaking free from the game's rules
quotes.excerpt: I always am trying to think about how can I break free from the game.
quotes.quote: I always am trying to think about how can I break free from the game because like some of the rules of the games have changed. They continuously change every day. So I think sometimes we are afraid of stuff from the old model of the game and we bring our fears from the old model of the game to the new model of the game and the new model of the game work completely different.

quotes.speaker: Jaylen Brown
quotes.summary_phrase: Jaylen Brown on the benefits of live streaming for his brand
quotes.excerpt: nothing is programmed, nothing is scripted, nothing is edited. That's not the game for athletes.
quotes.quote: Me streaming, live streaming where nothing is programmed, nothing is scripted, nothing is edited. That's not the game for athletes. But to be honest, it's been one of the most added benefits into my brand in the last year and to myself, because I've been able to connect with my fans in a much more authentic way. And I get to tell my story the way I want it to be told versus how these other people trying to tell my story.

quotes.speaker: Jaylen Brown
quotes.summary_phrase: Jaylen Brown on the systemic barriers for players from his background
quotes.excerpt: there's so many systems that's designed to keep you just down
quotes.quote: There's so many systems that's designed to keep you just down, like the way just America, but the world work is so many systems in place in the music industry and sports and politics, in the medical industry and and the food. There's so many systems that's in place to make sure that people that come from where we come from is not supposed to win. So when you trying to maneuver and make it and be successful, it's like you working at double the gravity. It's like you got to, it's like it's twice as hard.

quotes.speaker: Lil Baby
quotes.summary_phrase: Lil Baby on shifting his focus from giving back to systemic impact
quotes.excerpt: I want them to focus on how we can take my non-profit and not people just like
quotes.quote: I told my team like this year like far as my non-profit, I want them to the the focus on that. Like focus on how we can take my non-profit and not people just like baby give give backs and baby do. Like I want it to be real philanthropy, like it's real jobs, the kids really can go somewhere and the young guys can really, and I'm actually working on that right now. Because once you learn certain systems, it might could be $100,000 that could change a whole system. But you just got to know that. That's the system.

quotes.speaker: Jaylen Brown
quotes.summary_phrase: Jaylen Brown on the importance of hiring people you can learn from
quotes.excerpt: I only hire people that I can learn from. So now I'm paying you, but I'm also getting
quotes.quote: I only hire people that I can learn from. So now I'm paying you, but I'm also getting something back. Because a lot of times, you know, people can do the job, you know, but nobody really want to work for real, especially in today's time. People want to do the least amount of work, get the most amount paid. And I get it. You know what I mean? It's just the world we live in. But if you're going to be hiring people and you're going to be trying to start a vision, hire people that you can learn from, so at least you're getting your investment back.

quotes.speaker: Jaylen Brown
quotes.summary_phrase: Jaylen Brown on the impact of his best friend's suicide
quotes.excerpt: 2018, my second year in the league, my best friend who I grew up with, he committed suicide.
quotes.quote: 2018, my second year in the league, my best friend who I grew up with, he committed suicide. And and like this is like my dog. We went to the same high school, played on the same basketball team. He was coming up in Boston and like just kicking it. And he was going through some stuff and I, he was telling me about it. But you know, I'm 19 years old, like I'm trying to figure it out. I'm trying to figure it out, so I'm also trying to, you know, I'm telling him like, bro, like let's just go out, have a good time, you know what I mean? Let's go, let's be out, like do some stuff, we you forget all about that. Thinking like that's the type of therapy that he needed. That wasn't the the therapy that he needed.

quotes.speaker: Jaylen Brown
quotes.summary_phrase: Jaylen Brown on the importance of self-therapy and mental health
quotes.excerpt: I think some therapists don't believe that self-therapy is a thing. I think it is.
quotes.quote: I think some therapists don't believe that self-therapy is a thing. I think it is. Some therapists will tell you you need a actual clinical professional to be able to give you advice about how to better yourself. And I agree to that to a certain extent. But when I look in the mirror as a man, like and I'm nobody can give you that. Man, you know what I mean? Like when you know like I need to change this, you know what I'm saying? It's going to get changed.

quotes.speaker: Jaylen Brown
quotes.summary_phrase: Jaylen Brown on the impact of winning the Bill Russell Finals MVP
quotes.excerpt: it's named after Bill Russell, the Bill Russell Finals MVP. And Bill Russell somebody who lived in Boston
quotes.quote: To get that award and it's named after Bill Russell, the Bill Russell Finals MVP. And Bill Russell somebody who lived in Boston that dealt with a lot of bullshit when he was here. He used to stand up for what he believed in and people treated him like shit. He won 11 championships. So to get that award that's named after him and they call my name to get it, that was probably one of my highest moments.
